neighbours.label: the word that opens the 'each part on its own' side of a comparison between a combination and its parts (' either' in 'better than either one alone', ' taking'/' buying' in 'than taking/buying each separately'); output promotes ' separately', ' individually', ' alone'
fire: The combined vaccine produced a stronger immune response than either shot given on its own.
Exercise plus diet lowered blood pressure more than either approach did by itself.
The alloy turned out to be far harder than either of the two metals alone.
Using both antibiotics cleared the infection faster than either drug used singly.
The merged company is worth more than either firm was individually.
The duet sounded richer than either singer could manage solo.
Therapy with medication helped patients more than either treatment in isolation.
The joint bid was stronger than either city could have submitted separately.
quiet: The updated vaccine produced a stronger immune response than last year's shot did.
Exercise lowered blood pressure more than the doctors had expected.
The alloy turned out to be far harder than ordinary carbon steel.
You can take either antibiotic with food or on an empty stomach.
The merged company is worth more than analysts predicted in spring.
The duet sounded richer than the recording from the first rehearsal.
Patients may choose either therapy or medication after the first visit.
The joint bid was stronger than the committee had feared.

notes: Card: ' either' x4, ' by', ' buying', ' taking' after 'than'/'compared to'. Probes: 'than either one alone' 0.93, 'than buying each item separately' 0.36; plain comparison 0.01, 'together or separately' 0.01.
